questions: Do line_loss_events on the s-bend and slalom fall from 1 per run to 0 with the ±0.06 m span?
Does max_error drop below about 0.06 m on the s-bend and slalom, or does it stay at the off-track floor?
Does the oval finish rate hold at about 95 percent, or does the wider span add steering oscillation (above about 0.3) that causes the oval to fail?
Does the 30 mm pitch cause a coarser signal on the bends, and is the sensor_weights scaling right for five sensors at ±0.06 m?

intent: Test the untested wider sensor span (x = ±0.06 m at 30 mm pitch, y = 0.04 m) on top of the iteration 9 platform, which is the only geometry change. Expected result: line_loss_events on the s-bend and slalom fall toward 0, max_error moves below about 0.06 m, and the oval finish rate stays at or near 95 percent. Integrator note: five sensors at these x positions need sensor_weights rescaled to the new spacing, for example -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, or a version scaled to the wider span. The sensor_weights are the Integrator's choice and are not set here.
learning: Iteration 9 showed that the controller change clears the line loss on the oval but not on the s-bend and slalom, where max_error stays at the off-track floor. The span is the last untested geometry lever. If the wider span also leaves one line loss per run on the harder tracks, geometry is exhausted and the remaining gain is on the controller. If the wider span clears those losses, keep it and stop changing body parameters.
rationale: Iteration 9 (the Integrator's controller change on the iteration 5 geometry) scored 363.7, up from about 53.6. The oval now finishes in 19 of 20 trials, with 0.1 line-loss events on average and max_error of 0.037. The s-bend and slalom still end off_track in every trial, with one line loss per run and max_error at the 0.062 to 0.063 m floor. So the controller change cleared the line loss on the oval but not on the harder tracks. My previous feedback set the rule for this case: if the line loss persists with max_error at the floor, geometry has no tested lever left, so try the one untested option, a wider sensor bar. Every earlier geometry test kept the span at or below ±0.04 m, and the 10 mm bar gave two line losses in iteration 0. The s-bend and slalom are the tracks where the line leaves the sensor span, so a span of ±0.06 m at y = 0.04 m gives the bar coverage of the tape at larger offsets. I keep the rest of the iteration 9 platform fixed (mass 0.4 kg, track 0.10 m, wheel radius 0.030 m, body 0.18 x 0.12 m, sensor size 0.016 m, y = 0.04 m), so any change in s-bend or slalom line losses is attributable to span. The off-track limit stays at 0.06 m because body_width cannot raise it. The Integrator must rescale sensor_weights to five sensors at the new x positions, since the signal is a reading-weighted average of the weights. I expect line_loss_events on the s-bend and slalom to fall toward 0 and max_error to drop below 0.06 m. I also expect oval completion to hold.
